items.english: "It is no use going on with such childish talk forever. We are to be parted again for a while, and will you show me such a face?"
notes: Speaker unstated; taken as Tsunao answering Mitsuyo in p74.

items.english: "No, whatever you say, I will not let you go, and that is that."
Tsunao said nothing and hung his head. Mitsuyo drew close and peered into his face, laying her lovely hand upon his knee. "Do you so much want to go home?"
notes: Source prints the name as steel Tsunao here and in p78; normalised to Tsunao as in the rest of the text.

items.english: Tsunao kept his lips shut and would not even look. "Then," Mitsuyo said innocently, bringing her face near, "will you take me with you? Eh? Do take me with you, will you?"
notes: Same name variant as p77; normalised to Tsunao.

items.english: "Well, shall we both just go home?" Tsunao suddenly raised his head, and a tender light flashed in his eyes at the same moment, but in an instant he was himself again. "No, that will not do. You had better stay here."
"Oh dear, you say that again. Very well. Then I shall go home by myself."
From a room some way off came the thick voice of a provincial guest singing about trusting all to an ivy wig. In the passage a masseur sank to his knees with his "A treatment for you?"
notes: Song fragment left literal; sense of the lyric beyond the ivy wig phrase is unclear from this line alone.

data.say: Drafted the Tsunao and Mitsuyo parting quarrel through to the masseur closing the scene.
